name: fuel_tank_car
source: PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7, test-only fixture for tests/determinism/test_worker_count_hash.cpp's F12 case and data/scenarios/vehicle_fuel_tank.json. Identical to tests/support/fixtures/vehicles/car_sedan_fuel.json (relative paths rebased to ../../../data/) except initial_kg is deliberately tiny (0.005 kg, capacity_kg left at the real 45.02 kg). C7 review round 1 (F4): the ORIGINAL rationale here ('an in-gear 0.03 kg draft never stalled, so stay in Neutral') was measured only for that 0.03 kg draft tank, not for the shipped 0.005 kg one, and does not hold for it - with the 0.005 kg tank IN 1ST GEAR (gear_request 1) from a standing start at WOT, the tank empties at ~1.1 s and the engine DOES stall at ~5.8 s, but via a different, MORE INTERESTING mechanism than plain fuel-starvation-in-Neutral: once the tank runs dry the engine can no longer hold the driveline's speed, engine rpm falls toward anti_stall_rpm, and the auto-clutch's anti-stall panic release (AutoClutchDesc::anti_stall_release_rate_per_s, ManualTcu's Launch-mode branch) dumps the clutch open before the wheels can drag the dead engine below stall_rpm - the car then coasts under its own momentum with the clutch open and the engine stalled. This exercises the anti-stall path itself, not just the fuel model, so the scenario/fixture were switched from Neutral to the in-gear variant. Measured (2026-09-28, current shipped engine/fuel data): 0.005 kg (shipped) in 1st gear - tank empty ~1.1 s, engine stalled ~5.8 s (comfortably inside the scenario's 10 s duration; see test_worker_count_hash.cpp's companion case for the exact recorded values). For context/comparison only (not exercised by any shipped scenario): the earlier 0.03 kg draft tank in 1st gear never stalled at all in 10 s (tank empty ~6.9 s, the car's own momentum then motors the driveline and the engine coasts well above stall_rpm through the closed clutch) - this is why the ORIGINAL C7 commit picked Neutral in the first place, reasoning (correctly, for that draft tank's much larger initial mass, but not for the much smaller shipped 0.005 kg mass) that an in-gear launch might not stall within 10 s at all. A pure-Neutral WOT rev of the shipped 0.005 kg tank (no gear engaged) also stalls, and does so through simple fuel exhaustion alone (the auto-clutch's Launch law fully closes the clutch in Neutral regardless of rpm - see manual_tcu.cpp's own comment on this - so Neutral's stall is never mediated by the anti-stall path); that Neutral coast-down's own empty/stall gap matches a closed-form estimate (integral of J/|m(omega)| from 400 to ~6450-6600 rpm, J=0.16+0.004+0.010=0.174 kg*m^2, closed-form 3.73-3.80 s) almost exactly, which is a useful independent cross-check of the idle-integrator/fuel-starvation coupling but is no longer what the shipped scenario itself measures now that it is the in-gear variant. shipped car_sedan_fuel.json's own full tank (initial_kg = capacity_kg = 45.02) is never touched, per PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7's explicit rule.
